chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Quraish demolished the Ka'bah, they found a stone in its foundations containing a writing which they could not read properly, until they called a man who read it, and it said: 'I am Allah, the Lord of Bakka. I sanctified it on the day I created the heavens and the earth, and I placed it between these two mountains, and I surrounded it with seven angels, encircling it.'

key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: The Ka'bah, the cube-shaped building in Mecca
key_terms.بَكَّة: Bakka, an ancient name for Mecca

ai.seo_question: What did the Quraish find inside the foundation of the Ka'bah when they demolished it?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the pre-existence and divine sanctity of the Ka'bah, asserting that its consecration predates the creation of the heavens and earth. It underscores the theological significance of the site as a sanctuary protected by seven angels, reinforcing its status as the spiritual axis of the world in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Numan, from Saeed Al A’araj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the Qureysh demolished the Kabah, they found a rock in its foundation wherein was a letter which could not be read properly, until they called over a man, so he read it, so there was (written) in it: “I<sup>azwj</sup> am Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! The Owner of Bakka. I<sup>azwj</sup> Sanctified it on the day I<sup>azwj</sup> Created the skies and the earth, and I<sup>azwj</sup> Placed it between these two mountains, and Surrounded it with seven Angels, encircling”’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Nu’aman from Sa‘id al-’A‘raj who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

when Quraysh demolished al-Ka‘bah, they found in its foundations a stone with a writing on it which could not be read properly. They found a man who was able to read and this was written on it, ‘I am Allah, owner of Bakkah, which I made sacred on the day I created the skies and earth. I placed it between these two hills and made seven angels to guard it.’”
